title: Microsoft Purview DLP: rules to auto-resolve and tag alerts
summary: The role requirement needs to be narrowed to the Purview DLP alert management dashboard: Defender documents different permissions for investigating DLP alerts. The roadmap dates and planned behaviour match the record, and the searches confirm the gaps concerning the new rules.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans DLP rules for handling predictable alerts in advance.
claims.quote: Alert auto-resolution & tagging rules let you tell DLP, in advance, how to handle predictable alerts.

claims.claim: Planned resolving rules keep unwanted alerts from reaching the triage queue.
claims.quote: Resolve alerts you don't need to see - e.g., Low-severity alerts for mail sent only to your trusted partner domains, so they never reach your triage queue.

claims.claim: Planned tagging rules let alerts be found and routed.
claims.quote: Tag alerts so you can find and route them

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: confidence
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe the planned business-needs auto-resolution and tagging feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "auto-resolution" "tagging" rules; Purview DLP alert auto-resolution tagging rules business process default roles licensing PowerShell. Opened dlp-alerts-get-started, dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started and dlp-alert-investigation-learn; no feature procedure found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the supported conditions for the new alert-handling rules.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert tagging auto resolution default roles permissions conditions resolved alerts retention. Read DLP policy reference search excerpts and the DLP alerts pages; policy-match conditions do not document the new alert-handling rule conditions.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how the planned alert tags are named.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "auto-resolution" "tagging" rules; Purview DLP alert tagging auto resolution default roles permissions conditions resolved alerts retention. Opened DLP investigation and Defender DLP investigation pages; custom incident tags are documented, not naming rules for this feature.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Visibility, searchability and retention of alerts automatically resolved by the new rules are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert tagging auto resolution default roles permissions conditions resolved alerts retention. Opened dlp-alert-investigation-learn and dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started; they give existing dashboard retention, not the fate of alerts resolved by these new rules.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk

claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert tagging auto resolution default roles permissions conditions resolved alerts retention. Read the roadmap and the DLP alerts and Defender investigation pages; default policy and Defender tuning documentation do not state the default of this planned feature.

claims.claim: No admin UI or API for creating the planned auto-resolution and tagging rules is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "auto-resolution" "tagging" rules; Purview DLP alert auto resolution tagging rules PowerShell Graph API create rules. Opened DLP dashboard, Defender investigation, Set-DlpComplianceRule and Graph Update alert; read New-DlpComplianceRule syntax; none documents these rules.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert tagging auto resolution default roles permissions conditions resolved alerts retention. Read Purview permissions search excerpts, DLP alerts prerequisites and Defender investigation roles; none identifies permissions for creating the planned alert-handling rules.

claims.claim: The workloads covered by the new rules are not specified.

claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to the new rules are not documented.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics beyond the roadmap targets are not documented.

claims.claim: Existing DLP alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.
claims.quote: Alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.

claims.claim: Existing DLP alerts can be investigated in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: DLP alerts can be investigated and managed in the Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard and in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Existing DLP alerts can be investigated in Defender XDR, with the built-in DLP alert tuning rule disabled as explained in the paragraph.
claims.quote: When the built-in DLP alert tuning rule is disabled, you can manage and respond to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) alerts and incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Defender XDR for investigating and managing DLP alerts.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard is the recommended location for investigating and managing DLP alerts.

claims.claim: The documented Purview dashboard procedure has an analyst set Status to Resolved after taking the required action.
claims.quote: After you take the required action for the alert, set the Status of the alert to Resolved.

claims.claim: The built-in Defender DLP alert tuning rule took effect in early October 2026.
claims.quote: A built-in alert tuning rule for DLP signals took effect in early October 2026.

claims.claim: The built-in Defender rule converts DLP signals to behaviors rather than alerts.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Defender XDR, the rule sets these signals as behaviors instead of alerts, so they don't generate alerts or appear in the incident queue.

claims.claim: Disabling the built-in Defender rule allows DLP signals to continue appearing as alerts.
claims.quote: To continue seeing DLP signals as alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR, disable the rule in Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning.

claims.claim: DLP alert management requires Manage alerts plus either DLP Compliance Management or View-Only DLP Compliance Management.
claims.quote: Permission | Defender Alert Access: Manage Alerts | DLP + Security; View-Only Manage Alerts | DLP + Security; Information Protection Analyst | DLP only; DLP Compliance Management | DLP only; View-Only DLP Compliance Management | DLP only.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with: "Microsoft Learn documents that access to the Microsoft Purview DLP alert management dashboard requires the Manage alerts role plus either DLP Compliance Management or View-Only DLP Compliance Management." This is the scope stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started; do not apply this combined requirement to Defender alert management.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn states that the existing DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.
claims.quote: The DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn also says audit log retention policy configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.
claims.quote: Your organization's audit log retention policy configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Defender portal already supports associating custom tags with DLP incidents.
claims.quote: Associate custom tags to DLP incidents and filter by them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions

claims.claim: The cited Graph Update alert reference updates properties of an existing alert object identified by its id.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an alert object in an organization based on the specified alert id property.

claims.claim: Updating an existing alert's status is a different operation from defining a rule that handles future alerts.
claims.quote: Update the properties of an alert object in an organization based on the specified alert id property. status: The status of the alert. The possible values are: new, inProgress, resolved, unknownFutureValue.

claims.claim: Microsoft documentation does not link existing alert-update calls to configuring the planned future-alert rules.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert auto resolution tagging rules PowerShell Graph API create rules. Opened Graph Update alert, Defender DLP investigation and Set-DlpComplianceRule; read New-DlpComplianceRule syntax. No linkage to configuration of these planned rules was documented.
